outcome: Every new store is provisioned from one template, so networking and security roll out consistently without slowing the opening schedule.
overview: Opening a retail store means ordering a router, a switch, access points and a firewall from four places, configuring each by hand, and discovering at the third store that none of them were configured quite the same way. Fortinet SD-Branch collapses that into one managed stack: the firewall becomes the controller for switching and wireless, so a store is provisioned from a template and its network security is not a separate build. The gain is rollout speed and consistency, which for a chain opening stores is a schedule problem before it is a security one.

benefits.text: A new store is provisioned from a template rather than configured device by device
benefits.limits: Template speed assumes the store build is genuinely standard; a chain with many store formats gets many templates, and the gain shrinks accordingly

benefits.text: Networking and security are one stack under one console, so a store change is one change
benefits.limits: Consolidation is also concentration: the same console is now the single place a mistake reaches every store from

benefits.text: Store networks stay consistent, so a fault at one store is diagnosable from the others
benefits.limits: The same operating system runs on the appliance, as a virtual machine and in cloud, so the capability claim survives a form-factor change; the throughput figure behind it does not, and must be re-sized per form factor

residency: Store traffic and management data stay within the customer estate; the management console can be hosted on-premises rather than as a service where residency requires it

notFor.situation: A chain already standardised on another converged branch stack
notFor.why: The value is convergence, and a second converged stack un-converges the estate

notFor.situation: Stores whose network is a single broadband router with no local systems
notFor.why: There is nothing to converge, and the stack costs more than the problem

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Fortinet implementation partner · Duration: 6–8 weeks to a pilot store and a signed-off template; rollout at an agreed stores-per-week rate
Support model: Vendor hardware and subscription support with an agreed replacement term for store hardware; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed branch operations.
1) Assessment — store format review, port and wireless density, uplink inventory
2) Design — branch templates per format, zone and port profiles, uplink policy, rollout rings
3) Pilot — one store per format built from the template and validated in trading hours
4) Roll out and hand over — chain rollout on the runbook, operations handed over
deliverables: A new store is brought live from the template without per-device configuration
A template change reaches a ring of stores and can be rolled back within the agreed window
Point-of-sale devices land on their defined port profile automatically at connection
